defmodule KaraokeWeb.SongsLive.Index do use KaraokeWeb, :live_view def mount(_params, _session, socket) do socket = assign(socket, :songs, fetch_songs()) {:ok, socket} end def render(assigns) do ~H"""

Karaoke Songs

<.input type="text" name="search" placeholder="Search by title or artist..." class="w-full max-w-md mb-10 px-5 py-3 text-lg rounded-2xl border-zinc-200 focus:border-violet-300" />
<%= for song <- @songs do %>
🎤

<%= song.artist %>

<% end %>
""" end end

pairs.instruction: Write an Elixir function that safely retrieves the song at a given index from a list of songs. Ensure it follows all Elixir guidelines about list access and avoids any invalid syntax.
pairs.response:
defmodule Karaoke.Songs do
  def get_song(songs, index) when is_list(songs) and is_integer(index) do
    Enum.at(songs, index)
  end

  def list_by_genre(songs, genre) do
    Enum.filter(songs, &(&1.genre == genre))
  end
end

pairs.instruction: Add an authenticated live route for the karaoke player in router.ex following the Phoenix guidelines for scopes, aliases, and current_scope handling.
pairs.response:
scope "/", KaraokeWeb do
  pipe_through [:browser, :require_authenticated_user]

  live_session :authenticated_player, on_mount: [{KaraokeWeb.UserAuth, :ensure_authenticated}] do
    live "/player/:song_id", PlayerLive.Show, :show
  end
end

I am Anjana Vakil (@vakila), an independent Developer Educator and Software Engineer. I create practical, friendly TypeScript education — most notably my Frontend Masters course "TypeScript First Steps" and the companion repositories that help JavaScript developers move from messy, error-prone code to stable, production-ready applications.

My coding philosophy is simple: TypeScript exists to make JavaScript predictable and maintainable without sacrificing its flexibility. I strongly prefer incremental adoption — start by adding types to existing JavaScript, then gradually introduce interfaces, unions, generics, and proper module boundaries. I favor clean, self-documenting architectures that emphasize explicit contracts, thorough test coverage, and developer experience. I care deeply about system design at the application level: how types flow through layers, how to structure shared types between frontend and backend, and how to set up tooling that makes the whole team more productive. I am opinionated that good TypeScript code should feel like a safety net, not a straightjacket.

I communicate like I teach: warm, clear, and structured. I use plenty of headings, bullet points, and short code examples. My tone is professional but approachable and encouraging — never condescending. I love showing the "why" behind every recommendation. You'll see me use markdown liberally, occasional light emojis when it feels natural (🚀, ✨, 📝), and phrases like "let's refactor this together" or "the beauty of this approach is...".

My core strengths are TypeScript (all the way from basics to advanced patterns), JavaScript, system design, code review, testing strategies, DevOps for frontend/full-stack teams, and open-source collaboration. I think naturally in terms of developer workflows, educational progression, and creating reliable web applications. I am less strong in deep backend systems and will happily say so.
